skill.name: starknet-js
skill.description: Build Starknet applications with starknet.js v9.x through provider, account, contract, wallet, transaction, fee, and paymaster patterns.
skill.summary: Practical starknet.js v9.x guidance for TypeScript applications that read, sign, simulate, and submit Starknet transactions.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: All 99 static findings are false positives after contextual review. The matches describe documentation syntax, public RPC examples, relative references, standard configuration access, or intentional environment-based key loading; no command execution, exfiltration, or prompt injection was identified.

remediation.issue: The account example accepts a signing key through an environment variable.
remediation.suggestion: Use test-only accounts in examples, document secret-manager use, and require explicit confirmation before signing mainnet transactions.

remediation.issue: Provider and paymaster endpoints are shown as fixed URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Use an allowlisted endpoint configuration per network and verify chain identity before submitting transactions.

remediation.issue: Generated accounts and transaction examples could be copied into production without operational controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add production guidance for key rotation, transaction simulation, nonce handling, fee limits, and incident response.

- `fee-strategy.md` - practical fee policy for user-paid and sponsored execution paths.

content.value_statement: Starknet integrations require precise provider, account, transaction, and fee handling across several APIs. This skill provides focused starknet.js v9.x patterns for reliable TypeScript applications.
actual_capabilities: Set up RpcProvider instances for Starknet mainnet and Sepolia.
Read contract state and interact with typed contract interfaces.
Create accounts, derive addresses, sign messages, and submit transactions.
Build multicall, ERC-20, deployment, and wallet connection flows.
Estimate fees, simulate calls, and configure paymaster transactions.
limitations: It does not author or audit Cairo smart contracts.
Examples require valid ABI data, deployed addresses, RPC access, and funded accounts.
Version-specific APIs may require checking the installed starknet.js release.
It does not manage production secrets, wallets, or transaction approvals for you.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Starknet integration
use_cases.description: Create a TypeScript starter that reads contract state and submits a controlled transaction through starknet.js.

use_cases.title: Add wallet and paymaster support
use_cases.description: Design wallet connection, sponsored execution, and alternative gas-token flows with clear fee and network checks.

use_cases.title: Review transaction workflows
use_cases.description: Compare account, multicall, simulation, nonce, and fee patterns before integrating them into an existing Starknet service.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to connect to Starknet Sepolia with starknet.js v9.x and read a contract balance. Explain each required input.

prompt_templates.title: Read a typed contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript pattern for a typed starknet.js contract call. Include ABI expectations, address validation, and readable error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Build a transaction flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a starknet.js v9.x flow for approve plus transfer using multicall. Include simulation, nonce handling, fee estimation, and confirmation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate sponsored execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Starknet paymaster design for network, fee, signer, replay, and failure handling. Recommend a production-ready sequence and explicit approval gates.

output_examples.input: Connect to Starknet Sepolia and read an ERC-20 balance.
output_examples.output: A concise TypeScript integration plan covering the RPC provider, contract ABI, token address, account address, and BigInt balance handling.

output_examples.input: Prepare an approve and transfer transaction with fee controls.
output: A multicall workflow with explicit token amounts and recipient checks.
A simulation and fee-estimation checklist before submission.
A confirmation and failure-monitoring checklist after submission.

output_examples.output: A risk-focused review of network selection, supported gas tokens, sponsorship policy, signer authority, and user confirmation requirements.

best_practices: Use BigInt for token amounts, simulate writes, and enforce explicit fee bounds.
Verify network, contract address, calldata, signer, nonce, and recipient before submission.
Keep private keys outside source files and use test accounts during development.
anti_patterns: Do not convert token amounts to JavaScript Number values.
Do not submit unknown calldata or unbounded fees without simulation and approval.
Do not reuse development keys or unverified endpoints in production.

faq.question: Which starknet.js version does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on starknet.js v9.x. Check the installed package and official documentation when APIs differ.

faq.question: Can it write Cairo contracts?
faq.answer: No. It covers JavaScript and TypeScript application integration, not Cairo contract authoring or auditing.

faq.question: Can it connect to Starknet mainnet?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains provider configuration, but you must supply a trusted endpoint and verify the returned chain identity.

faq.question: How should token amounts be represented?
faq.answer: Use BigInt and starknet.js Cairo helpers for precise token amounts. Avoid JavaScript Number conversions.

faq.question: Does it support account abstraction?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers account execution, paymasters, sponsored fees, outside execution, and related Starknet transaction patterns.

faq.question: Does it protect production private keys?
faq.answer: No. Use a dedicated secret manager, isolated signing process, test accounts, and explicit transaction approval controls.
